_README: Error rates for the rules that decide what the Index publishes. Each was measured against a hand-judged sample drawn by seeded shuffle; `npm run validate -- --full` redraws the same samples. Intervals are Wilson 95%.

overExclusion.how: full census of every withdrawn domain; homepage fetched, title and description read by hand

underExclusion.how: `npm run probe-filter` and `SEED=1337 npm run probe-filter` — two draws, 66 each, 130 distinct domains (2 overlap). A domain is called unreadable only after three surfaces give nothing: homepage on the auditor's bot UA, the same request on a browser UA, then robots.txt and sitemap.xml at HTTP 200, whose URL paths name what a site is made of. Body text scanned for adult, gambling and piracy vocabulary; every hit hand-judged.
underExclusion.tiers: 100 judged on page body, 21 on robots/sitemap only, 9 on nothing. If the 21 robots/sitemap judgements are not trusted either, the worst case becomes 30/130 = 23.1%, 95% CI 16.6-31.1%.
underExclusion.flagged: 10 hits across both draws, all rejected by hand: XXX is the ISO 4217 code for no currency (xe.com), 'slots' are memory slots (asus.com), portals run casual Jackpot games (gmx.net, libero.it, web.de), a newspaper reported a burglary at a bingo hall (nine.com.au), an OnlyFans obituary (infobae.com), hotels near casinos in a sitemap (skyscanner.net), an ad-slot CSS class (archdaily.com), and polybuzz.ai's own FAQ saying it bans public NSFW.

wholePopulationBound.how: assume every domain that stayed unreadable is a wrong keep: allegro.pl, britishairways.com, dickssportinggoods.com, discogs.com, eltiempo.es, iau.ir, lowes.com, macys.com, viator.com — all answer automated clients with a Cloudflare or Akamai wall.
wholePopulationBound.says: at the far edge of the interval, at most 12.6% of kept domains are wrongly kept. This is the bound that faces the whole population, not just the part that could be read.

control.what: whether sites in the filtered categories wall bots more than other sites — the premise that made pursuing the unreadable domains worth doing rather than discarding them
control.measured: `POOL=withdrawn npm run probe-filter` — the identical procedure over 66 of the 357 removed domains: 9 unreadable, 13.6%, against 6.9% on the kept side.
control.verdict: NOT established. The difference is +6.7 percentage points, 95% CI -2.6 to +16.1, Fisher exact p = 0.189. It points the way the argument assumed, and it is within sampling noise. The pass is still worth it on its own terms — it cut the unmeasured share from a third to 7% — but the correlation is an open question, not evidence.

underExclusion.limits: The vocabulary scan reads raw page text including leaked CSS and JS, which costs false alarms and is why every hit is hand-judged rather than applied. The readable threshold counts prose words only — tokens with braces, semicolons or slashes are not words — so a homepage carrying 2,000 words of bundled JavaScript and no sentences counts as unreadable rather than as clean.
underExclusion.supersedes: 0/44 readable, CI 0-8.0%, which covered the readable population only and left a third of the sample unmeasured; and the single-seed 0/61 with a 16.5% worst case, which rested on one draw.

inSample.how: seed 42, 15 sites x 4 categories — the set the rule was tuned against, so not evidence of accuracy

heldOut.how: seed 99, disjoint from seed 42, 10 readable sites x 4 categories
heldOut.note: SUPERSEDED as the current rate by heldOutPostFix. Retained because it is what the rule scored before clarin.com and grow.google were fixed.

heldOutPostFix.how: seed 777, disjoint from seeds 42 and 99; 14 readable sites x 4 categories, judged by hand
heldOutPostFix.note: measured after the clarin.com and grow.google fixes. Pre-fix on seed 99 the held-out rate was 10%.
heldOutPostFix.checked: mega.nz 0/20 and bankofamerica.com 5/20 looked like under-credits and were verified correct: mega.nz serves a one-word JS shell, bankofamerica.com links no privacy page from its homepage HTML.

falsePositive.note: three detections is too few to support a rate; each was hand-checked against platform runtime config, not the detector's own patterns

shopMembership.how: seed 11, 20 domains marked shop, judged by hand
shopMembership.boundary: A shop is a site whose primary purpose is selling goods or services to the public and where a visitor can start a purchase. News, reference, social, government, sport, banking and free tools are not shops even when they sell a subscription. Whether to narrow this to retail only is a product decision, not a measurement one.
